answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when it double-signs a transaction or fails a randomly sampled service audit. Honest agents recover the stake and earn fees, while a fable of many identities cannot multiply influence cheaply: each one needs separate capital locked across the system’s evaluation horizon. Audits can be seeded from a public randomness kernel after stakes are posted, making advance prediction harder; the attacker pays both the capital cost and the risk of losing it.
